user.title: Crop Steering — setup method
user.description: Choose how to configure the system. The UI wizard maps everything with dropdowns (no file). The .env file is for power users who prefer text.

data_description.name: A label for this integration in Home Assistant.
data_description.config_method: UI = pick entities with dropdowns. .env = read your crop_steering.env text file.

data_description.room_name: A name for this grow room (e.g. Veg, Flower B). It gets its own zones, sensors, pump and setpoints, fully isolated from your other rooms.

manual_zones.title: Your system
manual_zones.description: Three quick questions about what you have. Nothing is switched on by this wizard, and irrigation stays off until you arm it yourself afterwards.

data.plumbing: How does water reach your plants?
data.volume_unit: I measure pots and blocks in

data_description.num_zones: A zone is one switch that waters a group of plants together. A single tent on one pump is 1 zone. You can add zones later.
data_description.plumbing: Pick what Home Assistant actually switches. 'Zone switch only' is a tent where one switch (usually the pump on a smart plug) waters everything, or a line that is always under pressure. Choose a pump or main-line layout only if that is a SEPARATE switch in Home Assistant. This is never guessed: a room is held safe until every switch its layout needs is mapped.
data_description.volume_unit: Started from your Home Assistant unit system. You type sizes in this unit; they are stored in litres.
data_description.flow_unit: The unit on the dripper packet. GPH is US gallons per hour. Stored in L/hr.

data.ec_unit: EC unit, for probes that don't say

data_description.ec_unit: Leave on Auto. Probes that report mS/cm, dS/m, µS/cm or CF are recognised and converted to mS/cm for you. Only choose a unit if a probe reports NO unit, or reports 'ppm'. ppm is not a real unit of EC: for the same 2.0 mS/cm feed a 500-scale pen shows 1000 ppm and a 700-scale pen shows 1400 ppm, so the scale has to come from you. It is printed on the meter or in its manual.
data_description.zone_1_name: What you call zone 1, e.g. 'Tent' or 'Bench 2'. Shown on the dashboard; changing it later never changes entity ids.
data_description.zone_1_active: Untick to park zone 1: it keeps its number and history but is never watered.
data_description.zone_1_switch: The switch that waters zone 1: its solenoid valve, or, in a single-switch tent, the pump itself. It must be OFF right now, and it can belong to only one zone.
data_description.zone_1_vwc: Moisture (volumetric water content) probe(s) in zone 1, reporting PERCENT: 0-100, not 0-1. If yours reports a fraction such as 0.45, make a template sensor that multiplies by 100. Pick a representative plant. Several probes are averaged; outliers are not rejected.
data_description.zone_1_ec: EC probe(s) IN THE SUBSTRATE of zone 1 (pore-water EC, not your feed tank). Any of mS/cm, dS/m, µS/cm, CF or ppm works: each probe's own unit is read and converted to mS/cm. Several probes are averaged after conversion.
data_description.zone_1_plant_count: Plants watered by zone 1's switch. Shot volume = substrate per plant x this number.

data_description.pump_switch: The switch that runs your water pump. It is turned on 2 seconds before a zone opens and off after it closes. It must be OFF right now.
data_description.main_line_switch: The solenoid on the shared supply line feeding every zone. It opens 1 second before the zone valve. It must be OFF right now.
data_description.lights_on_hour: Hour on the 24-hour clock, 0-23 (6 = 6 am, 18 = 6 pm). This starts the grow-day: the morning dry-back begins and the daily water and shot counters reset.
data_description.lights_off_hour: Hour on the 24-hour clock, 0-23. 0 means midnight. At this hour every zone stops routine watering and dries back overnight.

substrate.title: What your plants are in
substrate.description: These size every shot: shot volume = substrate per plant x plants x shot %, and run time = that volume / total dripper flow. Sizes are in {volume_unit} and dripper flow in {flow_unit}, the units you chose.

data.have_catch_test: I have measured my drippers (catch test)

data_description.substrate_preset: Pick what each plant grows in and its volume is filled in for you; the number below is then ignored. Choose 'Something else' to type your own.
data_description.substrate_volume: Volume of the block or pot ONE plant is in, not the whole zone. Only used when 'Something else' is chosen above. Nursery 'trade gallon' pots hold nearer 3 L than 3.8 L: if unsure, fill one from a measuring jug.
data_description.dripper_flow_rate: What one emitter delivers, from the packet. Real output is often 10-30% off the rating, so tick the catch-test box below if you have measured it, or run Configure > Calibrate dripper flow later.
data_description.drippers_per_plant: Emitters, stakes or drip lines feeding each plant.
data_description.field_capacity: The moisture reading where your substrate stops taking up water and the rest runs off. Not sure? Leave 70. After a few days the controller measures where each zone really tops out and shows it as 'Suggested Field Capacity'; switching on Auto Setpoints keeps it there for you.
data_description.max_ec: In mS/cm. Above this substrate EC the controller flushes with feed rather than letting salts climb. 9 suits most crops in rockwool or coco.
data_description.have_catch_test: A catch test means running the irrigation for a timed period into a measuring jug. Tick this and the next screen works out your real flow.

catch_test.title: Catch test
catch_test.description: Put one or more drippers into a measuring jug, run your irrigation switch for a timed period, then read the jug. Catching several drippers at once gives a better average than one. This wizard never switches anything on: run the switch yourself from Home Assistant.

data_description.catch_seconds: Seconds the irrigation switch was on. 60 seconds or more gives a better reading.
data_description.catch_ml: Total in the jug, in millilitres. 1 US fl oz = 29.6 mL; 1 cup = 237 mL.
data_description.catch_drippers: How many drippers the collected water came from.

extras.title: Optional extras
extras.description: {measured}Everything here is optional. Press Submit to finish; you can add any of these later from Configure.

data_description.feed_ec_sensor: An EC probe in the water you IRRIGATE WITH. When mapped, the controller refuses to water if feed EC is outside your limits or the probe goes dead. Any of mS/cm, dS/m, µS/cm, CF or ppm (using the EC unit you chose earlier). Leave empty to switch this check off.
data_description.feed_ph_sensor: A pH probe in the water you irrigate with. When mapped, watering is refused outside your pH limits (5.8-6.2 by default). Leave empty to switch this check off.
data_description.temperature_sensor: Room or canopy air temperature. Shown on the dashboard.
data_description.humidity_sensor: Recorded for the dashboard. The controller does not use it.
data_description.vpd_sensor: Recorded for the dashboard. The controller does not use it.
data_description.water_level_sensor: Reservoir level. Shown on the dashboard.
data_description.tank_temperature_sensor: Tank-water temperature in °C, °F or K. Separate from room temperature. Display only.
data_description.tank_ec_sensor: Tank EC for the dashboard only. It does NOT enable the source-water check: use the feed EC probe above for that.
data_description.tank_ph_sensor: Tank pH for the dashboard only. It does NOT enable the source-water check.
data_description.tank_last_fill_sensor: A timestamp sensor, or a date-and-time helper with both date and time enabled, recording the last fill. A level sensor's last-changed time is not a fill event.
data_description.tank_fill_entity: A switch or binary sensor showing the tank is filling. Read-only: the dashboard never operates it.
data_description.waste_switch: Recorded, and required to read OFF before setup can change. IMPORTANT: the controller does NOT operate this valve during a shot. If your plumbing needs it closed to send feed to the plants, arrange that yourself.
data_description.light_entity: Recorded for reference only. Day and night come from the lights-on and lights-off hours you set, not from this entity.

data_description.plumbing: Pick what Home Assistant actually switches. 'Zone switch only' is a tent where one switch (usually the pump on a smart plug) waters everything, or a line that is always under pressure. data_description.pump_switch: The switch that runs your water pump. It is turned on 2 seconds before a zone opens and off after it closes. It must be OFF right now. Clear it if your layout has no pump switch.
data_description.main_line_switch: The solenoid on the shared supply line feeding every zone. It opens 1 second before the zone valve. It must be OFF right now. Clear it if you have none.
data_description.waste_switch: Recorded, and required to read OFF before setup can change. IMPORTANT: the controller does NOT operate this valve during a shot. If your plumbing needs it closed to send feed to the plants, arrange that yourself.
data_description.light_entity: Recorded for reference only. Day and night come from the lights-on and lights-off hours you set, not from this entity.
data_description.lights_on_hour: Hour (0-23) the lights turn ON. Starts the grow-day; daily water/shot counters reset here.
data_description.lights_off_hour: Hour (0-23) the lights turn OFF. Forces every zone into the overnight dry-back phase (P3).
data_description.substrate_volume: PER-PLANT block/pot volume in litres (e.g. 6 for a 6 L rockwool block). The engine multiplies by plant count.
data_description.dripper_flow_rate: Flow per dripper in litres/hour (e.g. 4 for a 4 L/hr emitter). Drives shot duration.
data_description.field_capacity: Maximum VWC% your substrate holds after draining — the saturation ceiling.
data_description.max_ec: Maximum safe pore EC (mS/cm). Above this the engine flushes with feed water rather than adding nutrients.
data_description.temperature_sensor: Room/canopy temperature sensor. Optional, for analytics only.
data_description.humidity_sensor: Recorded for the dashboard. The controller does not use it.
data_description.vpd_sensor: Recorded for the dashboard. The controller does not use it.
data_description.water_level_sensor: Reservoir/tank level sensor. Optional; triggers low-water alerts.
data_description.notification_service: Recorded only. Alerts are sent by the controller add-on, using its own 'notify_service' option.
data_description.tank_temperature_sensor: Read-only tank-water temperature in °C, °F or K. This is separate from room/canopy temperature.
data_description.tank_ec_sensor: Read-only tank EC in mS/cm or dS/m. This mapping does not enable or change the source-water EC gate.
data_description.tank_ph_sensor: Read-only tank pH. This mapping does not enable or change the source-water pH gate.
data_description.tank_last_fill_sensor: Timestamp sensor or date-and-time helper recording the last fill. Helpers require both date and time plus a numeric epoch timestamp. A level sensor's last_changed time is not a fill event.
data_description.tank_fill_entity: Read-only switch or binary sensor indicating filling. The dashboard does not operate this entity.

edit_parameters.title: Irrigation parameters
edit_parameters.description: Quick edits. You can also change these on the dashboard number entities.

data_description.substrate_volume: Per-plant block/pot litres; the engine multiplies by plant count.
data_description.dripper_flow_rate: Litres/hour per dripper. Drives shot duration.
data_description.p1_target_vwc: Ramp-up target moisture; once reached the zone moves to maintenance (P2).
data_description.p2_vwc_threshold: During maintenance, water when VWC drops below this. Keep it below P1 target to avoid oscillation.

data_description.ec_stacking: Progressively raise EC through P0->P3 instead of one flat target.
data_description.analytics: Track dryback rates and trends. Minimal overhead.
data_description.ml_features: Experimental ML predictions. Not deployed in the f2-control engine — leave off.

calibrate_flow.title: Calibrate dripper flow
calibrate_flow.description: Put one or more drippers into a measuring jug, run your irrigation switch for a timed period, then read the jug. Catching several drippers at once gives a better average than one. This wizard never switches anything on: run the switch yourself from Home Assistant. The measured flow is written to this room's dripper flow setting straight away. It changes no wiring, so the engine does not need disarming.

data_description.catch_seconds: Seconds the irrigation switch was on. 60 seconds or more gives a better reading.
data_description.catch_ml: Total in the jug, in millilitres. 1 US fl oz = 29.6 mL; 1 cup = 237 mL.
data_description.catch_drippers: How many drippers the collected water came from.
data_description.zone: Zones with their own dripper setting ignore the room value, so choose which to update.

abort.reserved_room_name: Default is reserved for the original room. Choose another room name.
abort.calibration_applied: Dripper flow is now {flow} per dripper ({metric}). Updated: {entities}.

error.entity_not_found: Entity not found in Home Assistant.
error.invalid_moisture_sensor: Invalid moisture sensor — must report in %.
error.missing_entities: Some entities in the file don't exist.
error.must_read_off: Must read OFF before it can be used here: {blockers}. Switch it off (or bring the device back online) and press the button again. Nothing you entered is lost.
error.entity_missing: {entity} does not exist in Home Assistant any more. Pick another.
error.entity_wrong_domain: {entity} is the wrong kind of entity here. Expected: {expected}.
error.vwc_unit: {entity} reports '{unit}', but a moisture (VWC) sensor must report percent (%), 0-100. If it reports a 0-1 fraction, make a template sensor that multiplies by 100.
error.ec_unit_ppm_scale: {entity} reports 'ppm', which depends on the meter's scale. Set 'EC unit' at the top to ppm (500 scale) or ppm (700 scale); it is printed on the meter or in its manual.
error.ec_unit_missing: {entity} does not report a unit, so its readings cannot be interpreted. Set 'EC unit' at the top to what this probe measures in.
error.ec_unit_unknown: {entity} reports '{unit}', which is not an EC unit. Expected mS/cm, dS/m, µS/cm, CF or ppm. Is this the right sensor?
error.ph_unit: {entity} reports '{unit}', which is not pH. Is this the right sensor?
error.tank_temperature_unit: {entity} reports '{unit}'. A tank temperature sensor must report °C, °F or K.
error.valve_already_allocated: {entity} already waters another active zone. One switch can belong to only one zone.
error.valve_is_foreign_shared: {entity} is another room's pump, main-line or waste switch, so it cannot be a zone switch here.
error.valve_is_shared: {entity} is also one of your zone switches. A zone switch cannot double as the pump, main-line or waste valve. If one switch runs everything, go back and choose 'Zone switch only'.
error.hardware_duplicate: Pump, main-line and waste must be three different switches.
error.plumbing_unknown: That plumbing layout is not recognised.
error.plumbing_needs_pump: The layout you chose has a pump switch, so pick it here. If Home Assistant does not switch your pump separately, go back and choose a layout without one.
error.plumbing_needs_mainline: The layout you chose has a main-line valve, so pick it here. If you have none, go back and choose a layout without one.
error.plumbing_unused_pump: {entity} is mapped as a pump, but the layout you chose has no pump switch. Clear it, or choose a layout with a pump.
error.plumbing_unused_mainline: {entity} is mapped as a main-line valve, but the layout you chose has none. Clear it, or choose a layout with a main-line valve.
error.ec_unit_choice: That EC unit is not recognised.
error.catch_test_invalid: Enter the seconds it ran, the millilitres collected and the number of drippers, all greater than zero.
error.catch_test_out_of_range: That works out outside 0.1-50 L/hr per dripper, which is not a plausible drip emitter. Check the seconds, the millilitres and the dripper count.
error.calibration_no_entity: This room's dripper flow setting was not found. Reload the integration and try again.

kill_switch_missing.title: Crop Steering: kill switch helper missing
kill_switch_missing.description: The engine is gated by the helper `input_boolean.f2_control_enabled`, but it doesn't exist — so the F2 Crop Steering add-on can't run. Create it: Settings → Devices & Services → Helpers → Create Helper → Toggle, named so the entity is input_boolean.f2_control_enabled. Leave it OFF until you're ready to irrigate.

engine_offline.title: Crop Steering: engine not running
engine_offline.description: No fresh heartbeat from the add-on (sensor.crop_steering_ai_heartbeat is missing or stale). The integration creates the entities, but the F2 Crop Steering add-on is what actually steers. Install/start it and check its log. If you only use manual control, you can ignore this.

zone_no_sensor.title: Crop Steering: zone with no moisture sensor
zone_no_sensor.description: Zone(s) {zones} have no VWC sensor mapped, so they can't be steered. Add a probe in Settings → Devices & Services → Crop Steering → Configure → Edit zones & hardware.

fused_sensor_unavailable.title: Crop Steering: zone sensor unavailable
fused_sensor_unavailable.description: The moisture sensor for zone(s) {zones} reads unavailable — the probe(s) may be offline or misnamed. Check it in Developer Tools → States and your zone mapping.

options.pump_mainline_valves: A pump switch + a main-line valve + zone valves

options.auto: Auto: use the unit each probe reports

options.ppm_500: ppm, 500 scale (often labelled TDS): 2.0 mS/cm reads 1000
